sources.entry: GoAccess - Real-time web log analyzer and interactive viewer that runs in a terminal. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C

summary.one_liner: GoAccess is an open source, real-time web server log analyzer that shows interactive statistics in a terminal or as a live HTML dashboard.
summary.what_it_does: GoAccess parses web server access logs (Apache, Nginx, CloudFront, S3, ELB, Caddy JSON, IIS W3C and other formats, or custom format strings) and presents hits, visitors, bandwidth, response times, virtual hosts, UTM campaigns, bots and ASN data. Output goes to an interactive terminal UI by default, or to a self-contained HTML report that can update in real time over its built-in WebSocket server. It can also write JSON and CSV reports. Input can come from files, multiple logs, compressed files via zcat, or piped streams such as tail -f. Incremental processing lets it save a dataset to disk with --persist and append new logs later with --restore. Multi-threaded parsing is available with -j.
use_cases: Analyze web server access logs over SSH in a terminal
Generate a static HTML traffic report from nginx or apache logs
Monitor live site traffic in a browser dashboard
Spot scanners, bots and brute-force attempts in logs
Track slow requests and response times
Process rotated or compressed logs incrementally
notable: Real-time terminal and HTML dashboards that refresh every 200 ms (terminal) and every second (HTML)
Single-file HTML reports with no external file dependencies
Incremental log processing with on-disk persistence (--persist / --restore)
ASN-based exclusion of whole networks with --exclude-asn
Built-in WebSocket server with JWT authentication for live reports
caveats: Default in-memory hash tables limit dataset size to available physical memory
Runs on *nix systems; Windows support is only through Cygwin or WSL
Piped input does not prompt for log format, so the format must be set in config or on the command line
GeoIP2 ASN exclusion needs a separately supplied ASN database
